questions.question:
Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the following sentence meaningfully.

You all need to (get into) the books prescribed in your syllabus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'get into' should be replaced with 'go through' to convey the correct meaning.
 
• To **go through** a book means to read or examine it thoroughly, which is appropriate in the context of reading prescribed books in a syllabus.
 
• The other options do not fit as well in the context:
 
 
• **Read abreast:** This phrase is not commonly used and does not fit the context.
 
• **Read about:** This means to read some information related to the book, not the book itself.
 
• **Go about:** This means to start doing something, not specifically reading or examining books.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *You all need to **go through**__ the books prescribed in your syllabus*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When choosing the correct phrase to substitute in a sentence, always consider the context and the precise meaning that needs to be conveyed.
 
• In this case, 'go through' accurately captures the action of reading or examining the prescribed books thoroughly.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Ramu said that the dog had died in the evening.

options.text: Ramu said, “The dog die in the evening.”
Ramu said, “The dog died in the evening.”
Ramu said, “The dog have died in the evening.”
Ramu said, “The dog was died in the evening.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change the sentence from reported speech to direct speech,** we must carefully consider the original tense and person format.**
 
• The sentence** “Ramu said that the dog had died in the evening.”** is in past perfect tense.
 
• In direct speech, the past perfect tense converts to **simple past tense.**
 
• Therefore, the correct direct speech form is: **“The dog died in the evening.”**

**Correct Sentence:** ***"Ramu said, “The dog died in the evening.”***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The dog die in the evening."** – Incorrect tense.
 
• **Option 3: "The dog have died in the evening."** – Incorrect auxiliary verb.
 
• **Option 4: "The dog was died in the evening."** – Grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

His son thought, “If my father keeps grieving like this, the crops will die.”

options.text: His son thought that if his father kept grieving like that, the crops would die.
His son thought if his father kept grieving like this, the crops will die.
His son thought that his father kept grieving like that, then crops will die.
His son thought that if his father kept grieving like this, the crops would have died.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert from **direct to indirect speech**,** the tense may need to change**.

 
 
• **Here, the present tense ("keeps") changes to the past tense ("kept").**
 
 
 
• The** pronoun and words** indicating place or time may need to be adjusted **("like this" to "like that").**
 
• The future tense **("will die")** changes to the conditional tense** ("would die").**

Therefore, the correct indirect speech form is: **"His son thought that if his father kept grieving like that, the crops would die."​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "His son thought if his father kept grieving like this, the crops will die."** – Incorrect transformation of tense.
 
• **Option 3: "His son thought that his father kept grieving like that, then crops will die."** – Incorrect sentence structure and tense transformation.
 
• **Option 4: "His son thought that if his father kept grieving like this, the crops would have died."** – Incorrect transformation of the conditional form.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Mr. Deshmukh will be met by them at the site office.

options.text: They have met Mr. Deshmukh at the site office.
They will be meeting Mr. Deshmukh at the site office.
They have been meeting Mr. Deshmukh at the site office.
They will meet Mr. Deshmukh at the site office.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in passive voice. To convert it **to active voice,** the subject of **the passive sentence ("them") **becomes the object of the active sentence.
 
• The verb form changes from** "will be met" **in **passive to "will meet" in active.**
 
• The object of the passive sentence** ("Mr. Deshmukh") **becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct active voice sentence is:** "They will meet Mr. Deshmukh at the site office."**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: ***They will meet__ Mr. Deshmukh at the site office*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When converting sentences from** passive to active voice,** it's important to identify the subject, verb, and object correctly.
 
• In **passive voice**, the subject receives the action, whereas in** active voice**, the subject performs the action.
 
• Ensure that the verb tense remains consistent during the conversion.

questions.question: Why are the rivers called natural highways?

options.text: Because they link the towns and villages
Because they avoid overflow and flood
Because national highways are built alongside their banks
Because they enrich the beauty of Bengal and Kerala

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rivers** are described **as natural highways because they facilitate transportation and connectivity. **
 
• **They serve as natural routes for moving people and goods between different locations**.
 
• Historically,** rivers have been used for navigation, enabling trade and commerce.**
 
• The passage specifically mentions that** rivers **link towns with villages, highlighting their role in connecting different parts of the country.
 
• **This connectivity provided by rivers is vital for economic development and integration of regions.**
 
• Using rivers as highways can** reduce **transportation costs and time, benefiting both rural and urban areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **Because they avoid overflow and flood - This is incorrect as the passage mentions that rivers sometimes flood the countryside, indicating they do not always avoid overflow and flood.
 
• **Option 3:** Because national highways are built alongside their banks - This is incorrect as there is no mention of national highways being built alongside river banks in the passage.
 
• **Option 4:** Because they enrich the beauty of Bengal and Kerala - This is incorrect as although rivers do enhance the beauty of these regions, the term "natural highways" specifically refers to their connectivity function.
